Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 100, verse 1–11:

Tafsir of Surat al-'Adiyat

It is Meccan.

In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful

* *

Exalted is He swears by the horses when they are sent forth in His cause, running and snorting (ḍabḥ), and ḍabḥ is the sound heard from the horse when it runs. ﴿And by those that strike sparks﴾ meaning: the striking of their hooves against the rock so that fire is struck from it.

﴿And by those that attack at dawn﴾ meaning: the raid at the time of morning, as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to raid at dawn, listening for the call to prayer (adhan); if he heard it, he would hold off, and otherwise he would raid.

[And His saying] ﴿Then raise thereby clouds of dust﴾ meaning: dust in the place of the battlefield of the horses.

﴿And penetrate thereby into the midst of an assembly﴾ meaning: they all penetrate into the midst of that place, a gathering.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, ʿAbdah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from ʿAbd Allah: ﴿And the racers, panting﴾ He said: The camels.

And ʿAli said: They are the camels. And Ibn ʿAbbas said: They are the horses. The saying of Ibn ʿAbbas reached ʿAli, and he said: We had no horses on the day of Badr. Ibn ʿAbbas said: That was only in a detachment that was dispatched.

Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir said: Yunus narrated to us, Ibn Wahb informed us, Abu Sakhr informed me, from Abu Mu'awiyah al-Bajali, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who narrated to him, saying: While I was sitting in al-Hijr, a man came to me and asked me about ﴿And the racers, panting﴾. I said to him: They are the horses when they raid in the cause of Allah, then they return at night, and they prepare their food and kindle their fire. He turned away from me and went to ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him, while he was at the Zamzam water-station, and asked him about ﴿And the racers, panting﴾. He said: Have you asked anyone about it before me? He said: Yes, I asked Ibn ʿAbbas, and he said: They are the horses when they raid in the cause of Allah. He said: Go and call him to me. When he stood before him, he said: You give fatwas to the people about what you have no knowledge of. By Allah, if the first battle in Islam was Badr, and we had with us only two horses: a horse for al-Zubayr and a horse for al-Miqdad, then how can the racers, panting, be? They are only the racers, panting, from ʿArafah to Muzdalifah, and from Muzdalifah to Mina.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: So I retracted my statement and returned to what ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him, had said.

And with this chain from Ibn ʿAbbas, he said: ʿAli said: It is only ﴿And the racers, panting﴾ from ʿArafah to Muzdalifah, and when they reach Muzdalifah they kindle the fires.

Al-ʿAwfi narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas: They are the horses.

A group held the view of ʿAli, that they are the camels, among them: Ibrahim and ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr. Others held the view of Ibn ʿAbbas, among them: Mujahid, ʿIkrimah, ʿAta', Qatadah, and al-Dahhak. Ibn Jarir chose this view.

Ibn ʿAbbas and ʿAta' said: No animal has ever snorted (ḍabaḥat) except a horse or a dog.

Ibn Jurayj narrated from ʿAta': I heard Ibn ʿAbbas describe the ḍabḥ: "Ahh, ahh."

Most of these said, regarding His saying ﴿And by those that strike sparks﴾, meaning: with their hooves. It was also said: they kindle the war among their riders. This was said by Qatadah.

And from Ibn ʿAbbas and Mujahid: ﴿And by those that strike sparks﴾ meaning: the cunning of men.

It was also said: it is the kindling of fire when they return to their dwellings at night.

It was also said: the intended meaning is the fires of the tribes.

Those who interpreted it as horses said: it is the kindling of fire at Muzdalifah.

Ibn Jarir said: The correct view is the first, that they are the horses when they strike sparks with their hooves.

* *

As for His saying ﴿And by those that attack at dawn﴾, Ibn ʿAbbas, Mujahid, and Qatadah said: it means the raid of horses at dawn in the cause of Allah.

Those who interpreted it as camels said: it is the pushing forward at dawn from Muzdalifah to Mina.

And they all said regarding His saying ﴿Then raise thereby clouds of dust﴾: it is the place where, when they alight in it, they raise dust there, whether in Hajj or in a military campaign.

* *

As for His saying ﴿And penetrate thereby into the midst of an assembly﴾, al-ʿAwfi narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, ʿAta', ʿIkrimah, Qatadah, and al-Dahhak: it means the assembly of the disbelievers from the enemy.

It is possible that it means: they all penetrate into that place together, and ﴿assembly﴾ (jam'an) is in the accusative as an emphatic circumstantial qualifier (ḥāl mu'akkadah).

Abu Bakr al-Bazzar narrated here a very strange hadith. He said: Ahmad ibn ʿAbdah narrated to us, Hafs ibn Jumay' narrated to us, Simak narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent out horses, and they were away for a month with no news coming from them, so this was revealed: ﴿And the racers, panting﴾ — they panted with their legs; ﴿And by those that strike sparks﴾ — they struck stones with their hooves and produced fire; ﴿And by those that attack at dawn﴾ — they attacked the people by raiding; ﴿Then raise thereby clouds of dust﴾ — they raised dust with their hooves; ﴿And penetrate thereby into the midst of an assembly﴾ — he said: they attacked the people all together. [Al-Bazzar in Musnad, no. 2291, Kashf al-Astar; al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/142): "In it is Hafs ibn Jumay', who is weak."]

* *

As for His saying ﴿Indeed, mankind is to his Lord ungrateful﴾, this is the thing sworn about, meaning: he is indeed ungrateful and disbelieving toward the blessings of his Lord.

Ibn ʿAbbas, Mujahid, Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿi, Abu al-Jawza', Abu al-ʿAliyah, Abu al-Duha, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Muhammad ibn Qays, al-Dahhak, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, and Ibn Zayd said: al-Kanud is the ungrateful (al-kafur). Al-Hasan said: It is the one who counts the calamities and forgets the blessings of his Lord.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, ʿUbayd Allah narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr, from al-Qasim, from Abu Umamah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: ﴿Indeed, mankind is to his Lord ungrateful﴾ and said: "The kafur is the one who eats alone, strikes his servant, and withholds his gift." [Al-Tabari also narrated it in his tafsir (30/180) from Abu Kurayb, with the same chain.]

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it through the route of Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr, who is abandoned (matruk), so this is a weak chain. Ibn Jarir also narrated it from the hadith of Hariz ibn ʿUthman, from Hamzah ibn Hani', from Abu Umamah, as a statement of his own (mawquf). [Tafsir al-Tabari (30/180).]

* *

As for His saying ﴿And indeed, he is, to that, a witness﴾, Qatadah and Sufyan al-Thawri said: And indeed Allah is, to that, a witness. It is possible that the pronoun refers to man, as Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said, so its meaning would be: and indeed man, in his being ungrateful, is a witness, that is, by the tongue of his state, meaning that this is manifest upon him in his statements and actions, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿The polytheists are not to maintain the mosques of Allah while they testify against themselves with disbelief﴾ [al-Tawbah: 17].

* *

As for His saying ﴿And indeed, he is intensely loving of wealth﴾, meaning: and indeed he is intensely loving of good (al-khayr), which is wealth. In this there are two views:

One of them: the meaning is that he is intensely fond of wealth.

The second: he is greedy and stingy out of love of wealth. Both are correct.

Then Allah the Exalted said, discouraging attachment to this world, encouraging the Hereafter, and alerting to what will come after this state and what man will encounter of terrors: ﴿Does he not know that when what is in the graves is scattered﴾, meaning: what is in them of the dead is brought out, ﴿And what is in the breasts is obtained﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas and others said: meaning it is brought forth and made manifest what they used to conceal in their souls. ﴿Indeed, their Lord, that Day, is Acquainted with them﴾, meaning: He is Knowing of all that they used to do and work, rewarding them for it with the fullest reward, and He does not wrong an atom's weight.

End of the tafsir of Surat "al-'Adiyat". And to Allah belongs all praise and grace, and sufficient for us is Allah.
